# Orch v0.1.0

The first release of Orch: a self-hosted workspace where a team watches and steers coding agents together.
Organizations hold projects, topics and threads; each thread runs one agent (Codex, Claude Code or another
supported program) in an environment on a managed host or on a teammate's machine, with people's chat,
documents and approvals beside the work.

## Install

Download `orch-deploy-v0.1.0.tar.gz` and the server package for your architecture, unpack the deployment where
the system is to live, and follow `deploy/README.md` and the operator guides (`docs/operator/`): `update.sh
first-start` makes the secrets and starts the stack on Docker. Machines join through the connector downloads the
server carries for Linux, macOS and Windows (`docs/user/connect-a-machine.md`).

## In this release

- Organizations, departments, projects, topics and threads, with a permission page on every thing and roles
  that pages refer to. Sending to an agent takes Interact on the thread and Use of its model and of its
  environment; whoever lacks some of it asks for all of it in one request.
- Providers by subscription sign-in or API key, agent profiles, and environments on hosts or on a person's own
  machine; the connector uses the machine's proxy settings by default, and `orch-connector service install
  --proxy` / `--no-proxy` set its own.
- Live threads: queued inputs, steering, approvals, plan mode, sub-agents with their model and state, switching
  and forking between agent programs, and recovery after restarts and lost connections.
- Shared documents written by people and agents, people's chat, search, notifications and an audit trail.
